aspects.says: A builder checks rules that relate parts, and required parts, in build(), so the result does not depend on the order the setters were called in or on intermediate states.
basis: section:A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set

aspects.says: A builder names each part at the call site and gives optional parts defaults; it does not make the compiler reject a swapped value, which only distinct types do.
basis: section:Same-Typed Constructor Arguments Swap Without an Error; a Builder Names Each One
aspects.reason: naming and readability show at the call site, which a graded test cannot observe; the quiz checks the swap it addresses

aspects.says: HttpRequest.Builder.copy() gives each request its own builder with the template's state, so nothing added for one request reaches the template or the next request.
basis: section:HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

aspects.says: HttpRequest.Builder.header() adds a value, so a reused builder sends every earlier value too, while each built request keeps the state it had at build().
basis: section:HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

aspects.says: HttpRequest.Builder rejects a part that is wrong on its own at the setter call and leaves the missing URI to build().
basis: section:HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers
aspects.reason: this is the JDK's own behaviour, which a practice would test instead of the reader's code; the page shows the run and the Reference lists it

aspects.says: A product that keeps the builder's list, or an unmodifiable view of it, changes when the builder is used again; List.copyOf in the product fixes it.
basis: section:A Builder Used Again After build() Changes What It Built, Unless the Product Copies

aspects.says: For a small type, a record whose compact constructor checks its components does the builder's job, and a with-style copy goes through the same checks.
basis: section:A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set
aspects.reason: choosing a record over a builder is a design decision no test can grade; the page shows the run

aspects.says: A builder reused after build() keeps every part it was given, so each use of a template starts from its own copy of the builder.
basis: section:A Builder Used Again After build() Changes What It Built, Unless the Product Copies
section:HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

aspects.says: Two adjacent constructor parameters of the same type can be swapped at a call site without a compile error or a failing round-trip test, and the object is built with the wrong values.
basis: section:Same-Typed Constructor Arguments Swap Without an Error; a Builder Names Each One

aspects.says: A check in a setter compares against whatever has been set so far, so a cross-part rule placed there passes when the setters are called in the other order, and a missing part gets through as null.
basis: section:A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set

aspects.says: Telescoping constructors cannot give two optional parts of the same type their own overloads, because the signatures clash, so callers pass every positional value before the one they want.
basis: section:Same-Typed Constructor Arguments Swap Without an Error; a Builder Names Each One
aspects.reason: javac enforces the clash, so there is no wrong solution that compiles; the page shows the compiler error

aspects.says: Collections.unmodifiableList is a read-only view of the same list, so the builder's later writes show through it.
basis: section:A Builder Used Again After build() Changes What It Built, Unless the Product Copies
